problem_description: Compute the average temperature in K, pressure in bar, and coordination number in the first solvation shell for a system of glycine in water. The radial distribution function should be calculated in between the alpha carbon of the glycine and the oxygen atoms of the water molecules. The system should have single glycine molecules in a box of water (879 molecules) with dimensions of 3.0 nm x 3.0 nm x 3.0 nm. Periodic boundary conditions should be applied in all directions. The glycine should be modeled using the charmm27.ff force field, and the water should be modeled using the TIP3P model. First, energy minimization was performed using the steepest descent algorithm, where electrostatic interactions were treated using the Particle Mesh Ewald (PME) method with a Coulomb cutoff (rcoulomb) of 1.0 nm, and van der Waals interactions were computed using a cutoff of 1.0 nm. The system was then neutralized by adding appropriate counter-ions using gmx genion. This was followed by an equilibration phase consisting of two stages. In the first stage, a 400 ps equilibration was carried out in the NVT ensemble using the V-rescale thermostat to maintain the temperature at 300 K with a temperature coupling constant of 0.5 ps. In the second stage, the system was equilibrated for 500 ps in the NPT ensemble using the V-rescale thermostat and the Parrinello–Rahman barostat to maintain the temperature at 300 K (temperature coupling constant of 1 ps) and the pressure at 1 bar (pressure coupling constant of 5 ps). During both equilibration stages, electrostatic interactions were treated using the PME method with a Coulomb cutoff of 1.2 nm, and van der Waals interactions were calculated using a cutoff of 1.2 nm. Finally, a 2000 ps production run was performed in the NPT ensemble under the same conditions (with τₜ = 1 ps in the production run), where electrostatic interactions were treated using PME (rcoulomb = 1.2 nm) and van der Waals interactions were computed with a cutoff of 1.2 nm. All bonds involving hydrogen atoms were constrained using the LINCS algorithm, and a time step of 2 fs was used throughout the simulations. During the equilibration and production runs, van der Waals interactions were treated using a force-switch scheme (vdw-modifier = force-switch) with a switching distance of 1.0 nm and a cutoff of 1.2 nm, along with dispersion corrections applied to both energy and pressure (DispCorr = EnerPres). The average temperature, pressure, and coordination number should be calculated from the production run.
